note: Rio Grande NF near Cumbres Pass, ~10,000 ft, beside a meadow above Trujillo Meadows Reservoir (small motorized and non-motorized boats); the sites are set back from the shoreline. Reached from CO-17 by ~2 mi of dirt FR 118. An observation platform across from sites 40 and 41 looks out on a waterfall. --Claude
summary: FS page: confirmed 50 sites, max 40 ft, vault toilets, potable water, $29 (range $29-33 -> nightly_high 33), FCFS (no recreation.gov listing), 14-day limit; added season Memorial Day - Labor Day, sites 34-39 not RV friendly. Note cleaned of field facts. Pin fine; not waterfront kept.
flags: Phone: none stored. Conejos Peak Ranger District, La Jara, (719) 274-8971 (FS page, Office Contact Information). Suggest 719-274-8971.

Access road wording: the FS directions reach the campground by FR 118 ('Turn right onto Rd 118 and go 2.1 miles to campground on right'; from Chama 'go 2.5 miles north on Forest Road 118 to Forest Road 118.1B. Campground entrance is 0.3 miles north on Forest Road 118.1B'), with no 4WD, RV or trailer wording. But the same page's trail paragraph says 'Los Pinos Trail #736 can be accessed via the improved dirt Forest Road 1C and 4WD Forest Road #118.' That reads as the stretch of FR 118 beyond the campground toward the trailhead; the page does not say so. AWH may want to confirm the campground stretch is 2WD (memory user_ekko_no_4wd).
Rig length: the agency singles out sites 34-39 ('in an inner loop which are not RV friendly'); the stated 'Maximum site length - 40 feet' covers the rest. No criteria problem.

Status: FS banner 'Closed for the season- Will resume Memorial Day weekend 2027' (ordinary season end). Rio Grande NF conditions page (updated October 28, 2026) lists flood damage on Conejos Peak RD roads FSR 250, 128 (Elk Creek CG) and 105 only; nothing on FR 118 or CO-17.
Pin: stored 37.04650,-106.44972 is ~100 m west of the FS point (37.04676,-106.44862), both inside the upper loop on imagery. No recreation.gov catalog. OK.

Waterfront 'not waterfront' kept (checked both ways): on imagery the upper loop's north road is ~80-100 m from the reservoir across a band of dense conifers, so no lakefront and the view is at best partial through trees (lakeview not earned on imagery); the lower section is farther south. The Rio de los Pinos below the dam is creek-sized and 200 m+ from the FS point (NHD), ~70 m+ from the loop's east end across meadow. Neither earns a water class.
